name: application-response-viewer
title: Response Viewer
description: API response panel with a status-code badge, request timing and size, a copy action, and Body/Headers tabs — the body renders as a single formatted JSON block.
useWhen: Building an API client or request-testing tool (like a lightweight Postman/Insomnia panel) that shows the result of a request.
You need status/timing/size metadata plus a Headers tab alongside the response body.
Distinct from Json Tree Viewer, which offers per-key expand/collapse interaction rather than a status/timing header and body/headers tab switcher for an HTTP response.
avoidWhen: You need to explore deeply nested JSON node-by-node — use Json Tree Viewer instead.
There's no HTTP response context (status/timing/headers) — a plain code block is simpler.
responsiveBehavior: The body/header pre block scrolls horizontally on overflow rather than wrapping, preserving JSON/header formatting at any width.
accessibility: Status badge conveys success/error via both color and the numeric code plus status text, never color alone.
The Copy button announces its result via visible label text change ("Copy" to "Copied") rather than an icon-only state change.
Body/Headers tabs use aria-current to indicate the active tab.

variants.title: Response Viewer
variants.description: 200 OK status badge with timing/size, a Copy action, Body/Headers tabs, and a formatted JSON body.
accessibility: Copy button label switches to "Copied" as a text-based confirmation.

variants.title: Response Viewer (Dark)
variants.description: The same response panel adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Status badge and tab contrast remain distinguishable at dark-surface contrast.
